source.test: PaperDownloader.listVersions() empty-list guard vs NeoForge/Forge empty-after-filter guard

notes: Deliberately NOT unified, per P7.4's own instruction to characterize each provider's hand-rolled logic rather than paper over the differences. Paper's picker explicitly guards `!allVersions.isEmpty` (ServerJarProviders.swift:159-161) and throws a named error. Fabric's shared `firstStableVersion` helper guards the same way (line 509-511) since an empty list can never yield a version to pick. NeoForge's `latestStableVersion` has no explicit empty-list guard text at all -- it falls out naturally because `stable.max(by:)` on an empty array returns `nil`, which the `guard let best = ... else { throw .noStableVersion }` then catches (line 216-218); same effective outcome, different mechanism, worth a Rust port keeping the same shape (an `Option`/empty check vs a max-over-empty producing None) rather than a single early guard reused everywhere. Purpur's `listVersions` has no empty-list handling of any kind -- an empty (or 1.-prefix-filtered-to-empty) versions array simply produces a valid, empty `[ServerVersionEntry]` result, not an error; this is the one provider where an empty catalog is a legitimate, silent outcome rather than a failure.
